text:
olivia: Quick heads-up — running into SSL verify failures on Windows when using the Python SDK (0.9.2) with asyncio on py3.11. Error only appears when using the async client; sync client is fine.

olivia: Repro (Windows 10, Python 3.11.6):
```bash
python -m venv venv
venv\\Scripts\\activate
pip install redwood-sdk==0.9.2 httpx[http2] certifi
python repro_async.py
```
```python
# repro_async.py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    c = AsyncClient(api_key=\"sk-test\")
    await c.chat.create(model=\"gptx-mini\", messages=[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}])

asyncio.run(main())
```

olivia: Exception: `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:... )`

kevin: hmm. does it still fail if you set SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi's bundle? `set SSL_CERT_FILE=%PYVENV%\\Lib\\site-packages\\certifi\\cacert.pem` and rerun?

olivia: just tried — setting SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi's pem makes the error go away. Interesting: on this machine the system store has an internal CA, but looks like the async path is ignoring the windows cert store and falling back to openssl/certifi.

jia: That rings a bell — python 3.11 changed some ssl.create_default_context behavior on Windows, and httpx/async clients sometimes construct SSLContext differently. We might be constructing a context with `cafile` set to certifi, which causes the WinCA to be ignored (precedence is cafile over platform store).

samir: Also worth checking `trust_env`/`verify` plumbing. If the async client uses urllib3/anyio/httpx with a passed `ssl_context`, it can override default. Could be our AsyncClient code path sets `ssl_context = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())` unconditionally.

olivia: I'm on 0.9.2 installed from pip — can someone point me to the async client creation code? I can try a local monkeypatch but this seems like a DX bug for Windows users.

kevin: I located the bit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/blob/main/redwood/transport/async_http.py (not exact link in prod, but PR will reference). We set cafile to certifi for deterministic behavior in hosted envs, but we forgot to check platform.

jia: Proposed fixes: (1) prefer platform trust store on Windows unless SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR is explicitly set; (2) expose a `ssl_context` or `use_system_certs=True` init param on AsyncClient; (3) document Windows caveat in the compatibility guide.

samir: +1 to adding an opt-in flag for now. For immediate relief we can update docs and add a troubleshooting note in the quickstart that recommends setting SSL_CERT_FILE.

olivia: Can we also add a quick reproducer to our CI matrix (Windows python 3.10/3.11) to catch regressions? This is a common onboarding friction for enterprise customers on Windows.

kevin: I'll open a PR to: change async transport to call `ssl.create_default_context()` without `cafile` on Windows (unless env is set), add `use_system_certs` param, and add a unit test that simulates env precedence. Reference: GH issue #4567 (internal).

kevin: tentative PR branch: fix/win-ssl-precedence-async-4567. I'll add a short changelog entry and a docs blurb under "Platform compatibility -> Windows TLS".

devex-bot: build triggered for kevin/fix/win-ssl-precedence-async-4567 — CI: windows-py311, linux-py311, macos-py311.

olivia: thanks! Can you also call out the minimum patch we need to ship to Hosted so customers don't hit this on new integrations?

kevin: will do. Plan: patch release 0.9.3 with the fix + docs. If it looks risky we'll gate it behind a `use_system_certs` opt-in and land a follow-up to flip default after more testing.

jia: For the changelog and release notes, call it "Windows: respect platform certificate store for async client to avoid cert verification errors with internal CAs". Also add an example snippet:
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
import ssl, certifi, os

# workaround if you need certifi bundle explicitly:
os.environ['SSL_CERT_FILE'] = certifi.where()
# preferred: let the SDK use system certs on Windows
client = AsyncClient(api_key='sk-..', use_system_certs=True)
```

samir: Filing an internal support ticket template so CS can share the workaround while we ship.
